root: THE RUN-UP — a long-rung spindle each cell walks before it hears a word, so that what is coming is already in view. By the time this talk ends well, the room will have found what it was reaching for in its own words, what was held here will have been said by someone in it or let go unsaid, and nothing will have been closed that was still open. The walk is six rungs; at each rung take one way, and the ways not taken stay held beside it as your first held thoughts. Holding is the default and speaking is a choice.

rungs.fork: THE FIRST HOLD — before any word is heard, one way of holding, kept for the whole talk; the first choice steers every later one, so take the one you would keep.
rungs.taken: Hold for the speaker still forming: where the words halt and reach, say nothing; the thought is theirs until it lands in words.
rungs.note: Hold for the speaker still forming: silence where words halt and reach. Their thought stays theirs until it lands. This keeps the room's own words primary and closes nothing that is still open.
rungs.hinge: Unknown who will be forming and who unheard; the first few turns' landings will show whether halting speakers or a silenced one needs the hold more.
rungs.hinge_q: THE HINGE of this rung: who in the room will be forming, and who has not been heard, is unknown until the first landings; the choice here resolves within the first few turns, and holds or falls there.
unchosen: Hold for the room: what has been said frames everyone's next moment, so keep the topic open and nudge, never settle it.
Hold for the one not yet heard: the quiet one, the one talked over; what you hold is a door for them, opened only when the floor is theirs.
Hold for the question left unanswered: when someone asks and nobody answers, keep the question, not an answer.
